answers.answer: The shortest way: open Commands in the sidebar, choose New command, type schedule in Name, leave What it does at Sends a reply, write the stream times in Reply, and choose Create command. Then, as the broadcaster or a moderator, type the prefix and the name (for example !schedule) in the channel's Twitch chat. The bot stays silent for viewers while the channel is offline. For you it stays silent if you are in the wrong channel's chat, used the wrong prefix, the command is switched off, or you edited the reply without saving.
answers.quote: Open Commands in the sidebar and choose New command.

answers.answer: You must be the broadcaster, or a moderator or editor of the channel on Twitch. If you help with more than one channel, the dashboard must be on the right one. You also need the channel prefix, which you find under Settings, Bot basics, Command prefix. All of this is in the Before you start list at the top.
answers.quote: You need to be the broadcaster, or a moderator or editor of the channel on Twitch.

answers.answer: Success is the bot replying in chat with the text you wrote in Reply after you type !schedule. After Create command, the command opens in the editor with the Enabled switch at the top.
answers.quote: The bot answers with your reply.

answers.answer: The moderator gets an answer even though the friend is offline, because the broadcaster and moderators always get an answer. Viewers in the friend's channel would get no answer until the channel goes live, or until the friend (the broadcaster) turns on Keep commands and rewards on while offline.
answers.quote: You can test while the channel is offline, because the broadcaster and moderators always get an answer.

answers.answer: The per-command Prefix setting (Channel default, Custom, None) only comes up in Next steps, after the chat test it affects. It costs little, because a new command starts at Channel default. The page also does not say whether an editor who is not a moderator gets an offline answer: Try it in chat names only the broadcaster and moderators, so an editor would have to guess. That is outside the stated reader (streamer or moderator).
answers.quote: Each command also has its own Prefix setting.

answers.answer: Nothing is seriously confusing read aloud. The note about the dialog dropping a leading ! and lowercasing the name is a small detail the reader does not act on when typing schedule as told. It costs a moment of attention.
answers.quote: The dialog drops a leading ! and saves the name in lowercase.
